Data-Driven Stock Analysis 2024–2025

Kenet Kivimägi

Welcome

Explore our 2024–2025 data-driven stock analysis of U.S. equities. This tool highlights operational efficiency, predicted growth, and market performance. We combine firm productivity and predictive modeling to identify stocks with high expected growth and lower risk. All data is informational only.

Introduction

This section presents a quantitative analysis of selected U.S. stocks based on operational efficiency, investment activity, and model-based price predictions. Predictive Modeling

LASSO Model Prediction

Predicts stock growth based on historical data and company metrics. The LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression helps select the most relevant features while preventing overfitting.

We create a predictive model using LASSO to estimate expected stock price growth, combining historical financial trends with operational metrics. We train this model on past years and use it to predict growth for the following year. These predictions are designed to study relationships between efficiency and stock performance.

source("model_LASSO.R")

Productivity scores are plotted against the log value of actual growth of stock prices in a year. The results show that price growth is correlated with efficiency and this effect is present in every sector. What is specifically noticeable is that larger productivity scores reduce growth variance, in other words, risk. Lowered variance also means that the model has higher predictive power for firms which have high productivity and high market cap, since the error term variance is smaller.

For comparison, we plot the logarithm of the predicted stock price growth obtained from the LASSO model against the productivity values, showing a correlation between firm productivity and predicted growth. In the next section, we combine these two approaches to identify firms that are predicted to have positive growth while also having the highest possible efficiency scores. Note that the two graphs have different scales on the y-axis.

Disclaimer: Model outputs are projections only and should not be considered recommendations. Actual stock prices may differ significantly.
